Unit 27: Globalization, Cultural Homogenization, Multinational Corporations & Participle Clauses

👉 Hãy mở bài học bằng đường link https:// mà giáo viên gửi (bấm vào link trong Zalo ➔ chọn biểu tượng la bàn Safari).
Bấm để máy tự động đọc lần lượt từng từ và hiển thị theo dõi (phù hợp học trên điện thoại)
1. globalization (n)
/ˌɡləʊbəlaɪˈzeɪʃn/
toàn cầu hóa (sự hội nhập kinh tế, văn hóa và thương mại toàn cầu)
Collocation: rapid globalization, economic globalization, era of globalization
"Rapid globalization has interconnected national economies and transformed international trade."
2. multinational (adj/n)
/ˌmʌltiˈnæʃnəl/
đa quốc gia; tập đoàn đa quốc gia (multinational corporation / MNC)
Collocation: multinational corporations, giant multinationals, foreign multinationals
"Multinational corporations often establish factories in developing nations to reduce labour costs."
3. outsource (v)
/ˈaʊtsɔːs/
thuê ngoài, chuyển dịch sản xuất/dịch vụ sang quốc gia khác có chi phí thấp hơn (n: outsourcing)
Collocation: outsource manufacturing jobs, outsource customer service
"Many Western technology firms outsource their manufacturing operations to Asia."
4. tariff (n)
/ˈtærɪf/
thuế quan xuất nhập khẩu
Collocation: impose heavy tariffs, abolish trade tariffs, import tariff
"Removing trade tariffs between neighbouring countries stimulates cross-border commerce."
5. export (v/n)
/ɪkˈspɔːt/
xuất khẩu (hàng hóa ra nước ngoài — động từ nhấn âm 2 /ɪkˈspɔːt/, danh từ nhấn âm 1 /ˈekspɔːt/)
Collocation: export agricultural products, major export market
"Vietnam exports millions of tonnes of rice, coffee, and electronics to global markets annually."
6. import (v/n)
/ɪmˈpɔːt/
nhập khẩu (hàng hóa từ nước ngoài vào)
Collocation: import raw materials, rely on imported oil
"Countries with limited arable land must import a large proportion of their food supply."
7. homogenize (v)
/həˈmɒdʒənaɪz/
đồng nhất hóa, làm cho mọi nơi trở nên giống hệt nhau và mất bản sắc riêng (n: homogenization)
Collocation: cultural homogenization, homogenize global lifestyles
"Critics fear that the spread of Western fast-food chains will homogenize global cultures."
8. assimilate (v)
/əˈsɪmɪleɪt/
hòa nhập, đồng hóa vào một nền văn hóa mới (n: assimilation)
Collocation: assimilate into the host culture, cultural assimilation
"Immigrants often face pressure to assimilate into the host society while keeping their native traditions."
9. diversity (n)
/daɪˈvɜːsəti/
sự đa dạng (văn hóa, ngôn ngữ, sắc tộc — adj: diverse)
Collocation: cultural diversity, linguistic diversity, celebrate diversity
"UNESCO works to protect linguistic and cultural diversity across the globe."
10. erode (v)
/ɪˈrəʊd/
làm xói mòn, làm mai một dần (giá trị truyền thống, bản sắc văn hóa, lòng tin — n: erosion)
Collocation: erode traditional values, erode national identity
"The dominance of Hollywood blockbusters can gradually erode local artistic traditions."
11. prosperity (n)
/prɒˈsperəti/
sự thịnh vượng, sự giàu có phát đạt (adj: prosperous — thịnh vượng)
Collocation: economic prosperity, shared prosperity, bring prosperity to
"International trade and foreign investment have brought unprecedented economic prosperity to the region."
12. sweatshop (n)
/ˈswetʃɒp/
công xưởng bóc lột sức lao động (trả lương rẻ mạt, điều kiện làm việc tồi tàn)
Collocation: sweatshop labour, exploit workers in sweatshops
"Ethical consumers boycott fashion brands that exploit garment workers in unsafe sweatshops."
13. interdependent (adj)
/ˌɪntədɪˈpendənt/
phụ thuộc lẫn nhau (n: interdependence — sự phụ thuộc qua lại giữa các nền kinh tế)
Collocation: mutually interdependent economies, global interdependence
"In our interdependent world, a supply chain crisis in one country affects factories worldwide."
14. standardize (v)
/ˈstændədaɪz/
tiêu chuẩn hóa, chuẩn hóa theo cùng một quy chuẩn quốc tế
Collocation: standardize safety regulations, standardized products
"International organizations standardize aviation and shipping rules to ensure global safety."
15. indigenous (adj)
/ɪnˈdɪdʒənəs/
bản địa, truyền thống lâu đời tại địa phương (= native)
Collocation: indigenous languages, indigenous peoples, indigenous crafts
"Linguists warn that hundreds of indigenous languages could vanish before the end of the century."

⚙️ 2. Bài Giảng Ngữ Pháp 2 Tầng (Grammar Masterclass)

🟢 Tầng 1: Rút Gọn Mệnh Đề Quan Hệ (Reduced Relative Clauses: V-ing / V3/ed / to-V)

• Tại sao phải rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ? Giúp câu văn học thuật súc tích hơn và tăng điểm tiêu chí Grammatical Range & Accuracy (Band 7.0+):
  1. Rút gọn Chủ động thành V-ing (khi MĐQH dùng động từ chủ động):
    Gốc: Multinational corporations which operate in developing nations create millions of jobs.
    Rút gọn: Multinational corporations operating in developing nations create millions of jobs.
  2. Rút gọn Bị động thành V3/ed (khi MĐQH dùng who/which/that + be + V3/ed):
    Gốc: Goods which are manufactured in low-cost countries are exported worldwide.
    Rút gọn: Goods manufactured in low-cost countries are exported worldwide.
  3. Rút gọn thành to-V (sau the first, the second, the only, the best + Noun):
    Ví dụ: Singapore was one of the first Asian nations to embrace free-trade globalization.

🔵 Tầng 2: Mệnh Đề Phân Từ Đồng Chủ Ngữ Ở Đầu Câu (Fronted Participle Clauses — C1-C2)

• Khi 2 mệnh đề có CÙNG CHỦ NGỮ, bạn có thể rút gọn mệnh đề phụ ở đầu câu thành V-ing (chủ động) hoặc V3/ed (bị động):
  - V3/ed..., S + V (Bị động — Do được thúc đẩy bởi / Bị thu hút bởi):
    Ví dụ: Driven by lower labour costs, multinational corporations outsource manufacturing to developing countries.
  - V-ing / Having + V3/ed..., S + V (Chủ động):
    Ví dụ: Fearing the loss of indigenous languages, many governments fund cultural preservation programmes.
  Lưu ý sống còn: Chủ ngữ ngay sau dấu phẩy BẮT BUỘC phải là chủ thể thực hiện/nhận hành động ở đầu câu!

🎯 20 Câu Test Từ Vựng (Vocabulary Mastery Test)

1. Economic ________ has allowed consumers to buy fresh fruit and electronics from across the planet.
2. Giant ________ corporations like Apple and Samsung operate research centres and factories in dozens of countries.
3. To cut operational expenses, many Western banks ________ their IT support services to India and the Philippines.
4. Free trade agreements abolish import ________ so that goods can cross borders without extra taxes.
5. Vietnam is one of the world's leading nations that ________ agricultural products such as coffee and cashew nuts.
6. Because Japan lacks natural oil reserves, it must ________ almost all of its fossil fuels from abroad.
7. Sociologists worry that identical shopping malls and fast-food chains will ________ cities around the world.
8. Second-generation immigrants usually speak the local language fluently and ________ easily into society.
9. International festivals celebrate cultural ________ by showcasing traditional costumes, music, and cuisine.
10. Uncontrolled mass tourism and foreign media can gradually ________ traditional family values in rural villages.
11. Opening up to international trade has lifted millions out of poverty and brought economic ________.
12. Human rights groups campaign against fast-fashion factories that force labourers to work in dangerous ________.
13. Modern nations are so economically ________ that a financial crash in one country quickly spreads globally.
14. Shipping containers were designed to ________ cargo sizes so goods can be transferred between ships and trains easily.
15. Recording folk songs and teaching local dialects in schools help preserve ________ cultures from disappearing.
16. [Ôn tập Unit 26] It is ________ that space agencies cooperate to clear dangerous orbital debris.
17. [Ôn tập Unit 25] Mutual trust and shared traditions strengthen social ________ within a community.
18. [Ôn tập Unit 24] Excessive smartphone use before bed is highly ________ to sleep quality and cognitive function.
19. [Ôn tập Unit 23] Tabloid newspapers often ________ minor celebrity scandals to attract online clicks.
20. [Ôn tập Unit 21] By 2050, the working-age ________ in many developed nations is projected to shrink.
Điểm: 0/20

⚙️ 10 Câu Test Ngữ Pháp Ứng Dụng (Grammar Mastery Test)

1. Reduced Relative Clause (Active): Multinational corporations ________ in developing countries create millions of manufacturing jobs.
2. Reduced Relative Clause (Passive): Electronic goods ________ in Vietnam are exported to over one hundred countries.
3. Fronted Participle Clause (Passive): ________ by lower wages and tax incentives, foreign firms invest heavily in Southeast Asia.
4. Fronted Participle Clause (Active): ________ the erosion of indigenous languages, UNESCO launched a global preservation fund.
5. Reduced Relative Clause after Superlative: Britain was the first nation ________ industrial manufacturing in the 18th century.
6. ________ trade tariffs between ASEAN members has significantly boosted regional prosperity.
7. It is essential that every multinational corporation ________ ethical labour standards instead of using sweatshops.
8. By 2035, global e-commerce exports ________ to double in value compared to 2020.
9. Not only ________ globalization expand consumer choice, but it also promotes cross-cultural understanding.
10. The more interdependent national economies become, ________ vital international cooperation is.
Điểm: 0/10

Trade Fair Director: Good morning, Global Artisan and Cultural Trade Expo, Director Sophia Martinez speaking. How can I help you?
Craft Cooperative Manager: Hello Ms. Martinez! My name is Kenji Takahashi. I manage an indigenous silk-weaving cooperative, and I would like to rent an exhibition booth at next month's expo.
Trade Fair Director: We would be honoured to showcase your traditional crafts, Kenji! Could you spell your surname for our exhibitor contract?
Craft Cooperative Manager: Yes, it is Takahashi. T - A - K - A - H - A - S - H - I. 💡 Đáp án câu 1 (Họ người đăng ký): TAKAHASHI
Trade Fair Director: Thank you. Our expo connects local artisans directly with international buyers to protect cultural diversity and prevent sweatshop exploitation.
Craft Cooperative Manager: That aligns with our mission! Which hall should we book for handmade textiles and clothing?
Trade Fair Director: Food exporters are in the West Pavilion, while all traditional textiles and indigenous crafts are displayed in the Heritage Hall. 💡 Bẫy khu ẩm thực (West Pavilion) vs khu dệt may truyền thống câu 2: Heritage Hall
Craft Cooperative Manager: Heritage Hall sounds ideal. How large is a standard exhibition booth, and how much does it cost?
Trade Fair Director: A standard nine-square-metre booth normally costs 600 pounds, but certified fair-trade cooperatives receive a discounted rate of 380 pounds. 💡 Bẫy giá gốc (600) vs giá ưu đãi hợp tác xã câu 3: 380
Craft Cooperative Manager: Three hundred and eighty pounds for three days is very reasonable. Do you also offer seminars on international shipping and export rules?
Trade Fair Director: Yes! On Friday morning, trade lawyers host a workshop on how to export goods duty-free without paying heavy customs tariffs. 💡 Đáp án câu 4 (Miễn thuế quan xuất nhập khẩu): tariffs
Craft Cooperative Manager: That will be extremely useful for our weavers. How many international buyers are expected to attend this year's expo?
Trade Fair Director: Over 1,200 retail buyers from thirty-five countries have already registered. 💡 Đáp án câu 5 (Số lượng nhà mua hàng quốc tế): 1200 / 1,200
Craft Cooperative Manager: Wonderful! What is the deadline to submit our cooperative certificate and product photos?
Trade Fair Director: Please upload your documents to our portal by the 12th of November. We look forward to welcoming you! 💡 Đáp án câu 6 (Hạn chót nộp hồ sơ): 12th November / November 12

📰 IELTS Academic Reading: Passage & Questions

[Paragraph A - Economic Prosperity Driven by Global Trade]
Over the past half-century, rapid globalization and the abolition of trade tariffs have created a deeply interdependent global economy. Driven by lower production costs, multinational corporations have outsourced manufacturing to developing nations in Asia and Latin America. Products manufactured in these factories are exported worldwide, while raw materials and advanced machinery are imported across borders daily. Although critics condemn unethical companies operating unsafe sweatshops, international trade has undeniably lifted ratusan of millions of people out of poverty and generated unprecedented economic prosperity.

[Paragraph B - The Threat of Cultural Homogenization]
However, sociologists warn that economic integration carries a high cultural price. As giant multinationals standardize consumer products, fashion, and entertainment across the globe, distinct local traditions face the threat of cultural homogenization. Walk down the main street of any metropolis today, and you will see identical coffee chains, global clothing brands, and Hollywood films. Fearing that young people will blindly assimilate into a single Westernized lifestyle, cultural historians argue that unchecked globalization gradually erodes national identity and pushes indigenous languages toward extinction.

[Paragraph C - Preserving Cultural Diversity in a Globalized Era]
Fortunately, cultural erosion is not inevitable. The very digital technologies that spread global brands also empower local communities to showcase their heritage to a worldwide audience. Artisans weaving indigenous textiles can now export their crafts directly to ethical consumers abroad, while international tourism provides a strong financial incentive to preserve historical monuments and folk festivals. Provided that governments protect labour rights and educate youth to take pride in their roots, nations can enjoy economic prosperity while celebrating cultural diversity.
Điểm: 0/6
